findings.title: Coverage map leaves 17 spec acceptance bullets unowned while claiming Unallocated 0
findings.body: The map says it lists every acceptance criterion at the spec's own bullet granularity and reports Total criteria: 210. Unallocated: 0. Checking Spec A's Part 5 / FR-F6 numbered items plus every *Acceptance* bullet in specs/spec-a-doctrine.md and specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md yields 226 acceptance bullets; 17 of those have no map row. Spec A: FR-A6 'a convention at the launch word, never a check' and 'after the reset, no exemption for correctness'; FR-A10 'the tripwire on the pass itself'; FR-B3 'the line' (the six-field keep-or-retire entry); FR-B6 'the sentence layer', 'the glossary and stable slugs', and 'doctrine is cut where it is restructured'; FR-C1 'the decisions-asked count'. Spec B: FR-M1 'the closing rule: a one-time migration record'; FR-M2 'a tripwire firing separates what was observed from what it infers'; FR-M7 'the self-vouching KEEP rows'; FR-D3 'the consumer report's venue, format, and evidence bar'; FR-D9 'three answers owed now'; FR-S1 'entry-surface changes are announced, not aliased', 'the transport contract moves to each engine's native structured channel', and 'the benefit is priced, not promised'; FR-S8 'stripped changes are still reviewed'. The map also treats Spec B FR-S3's '*Consequence (owner terms):*' sentence as an acceptance bullet (FR-S3 bullet 3), which the spec does not mark as Acceptance. Several of the missing bullets are the actual work of existing children (C3's prose-standard.md is the sentence layer; C11's What is the native-channel ruling; C16's review-only file is the stripped-changes rule; C13's design note is the three answers), so the map's owner column cannot be used to grade those landings.
findings.suggestion: Add one map row per missing *Acceptance* bullet (suggested owners: C2 for the two FR-A6 bullets, the FR-A10 tripwire, and FR-C1's count; C6 for FR-B3 'the line'; C3/C1/C7 for the three FR-B6 bullets; C10–C13 for FR-M1's closing rule; C2 for FR-M2's readout; C10/C12 for FR-M7 self-vouching; C2 or C12 for FR-D3's consumer-report bar; C13 for FR-D9's three answers; C10 for FR-S1's no-alias rule; C11 for FR-S1 native-channel and priced-benefit; C16 for FR-S8 stripped changes). Drop the FR-S3 Consequence row. Recount against the specs, not the map.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-A6 has seven *Acceptance* bullets (map rows 33–37 cover five); FR-A10 has seven (map 46–51 cover six); FR-B3 opens with 'the unit' then 'the line' then 'condition shapes' (map FR-B3 jumps from unit to condition shapes); FR-B6 has nine *Acceptance* bullets (map 88–93 cover six). specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md FR-S1 has ten *Acceptance* bullets (map 198–204 cover seven); FR-S8 has four (map 216–218 cover three). package/coverage-map.md line 222: 'Total criteria: 210. Unallocated: 0.'

findings.title: C9 owns no coverage-map row; the trial criterion is assigned to C15
findings.body: Child C9 exists as the background-session trial (package/children/C9.md) and is named in sequencing as Wave 1 so its receipt can inform C15. The coverage-map Counts line lists every child except C9. Spec A FR-B6's *Acceptance (record, markers whose condition is met)* is the criterion that defines the trial: 'The receipt is the background-session trial … one wave on that path across all three accounts, against the failure classes the machinery was built for, recorded in LEDGERS'. The map assigns that entire bullet to C15. C15 is the decommission child sequenced after C9's receipt; it cannot run the trial. That is a mis-split whose declared owner cannot deliver the trial half, and it leaves C9 with no owned acceptance criterion to grade.
findings.suggestion: Split FR-B6 bullet 2: C9 owns the trial (wave, three accounts, failure classes, LEDGERS, no replacement code first); C15 owns the deletions that wait on that receipt. Give C9 a non-zero Counts entry.
findings.evidence: package/coverage-map.md line 89 owner column is '**C15**' for FR-B6 bullet 'six orchestration pieces have met their delete-when condition…'. Line 222 Counts names C1, C10–C17, C2–C8 and has no C9. package/children/C9.md What is the trial; package/children/C15.md Sequencing is 'Wave 3, after C9's receipt'.

findings.title: R15's 'six orchestration pieces' are not the six Spec A FR-B6 names
findings.body: Spec A FR-B6 *Acceptance (record, markers whose condition is met)* names the six retirement candidates as: detached spawn in the launcher; wave-watch arming and the re-arm ritual; transcript-mtime liveness; the turn-end doctrine with its 540 and 600 second slice recipes; multi-account provisioning transport; and the launcher-enforced half of the own-worktree ruling. Heartbeat, harness_probe, and quota are separate sentences in that bullet and in the next (quota) bullet. Register R15 instead binds C9/C15/C7 to this closed list: 'detached spawn in the launcher, the wave-watch re-arm, the heartbeat, harness_probe, the quota poller and preflight check one, and the wave-watch new-session-id roll'. That list drops four of the spec's six (transcript-mtime liveness, turn-end doctrine, multi-account provisioning transport, own-worktree half), inserts pieces the spec kept separate (heartbeat, harness_probe, quota poller), and adds a 'new-session-id roll' the spec never names as one of the six. C9.md and C15.md quote R15 and repeat that wrong census in What, so builders will retire the wrong machinery. Spec A Part 6 item 11 still distinguishes 'the six pieces whose condition is met' from 'the conditional heartbeat, the quota removal, harness_probe, and the wave-watch re-arm request's closure'.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite R15 (and C9/C15 What) to the spec's six plus the separately named heartbeat, harness_probe, quota, and re-arm-request closure. Do not treat quota poller as a sixth piece.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-B6: 'six orchestration pieces have met their delete-when condition and are retirement candidates behind one receipt: detached spawn in the launcher; wave-watch arming and the re-arm ritual; transcript-mtime liveness; the turn-end doctrine with its 540 and 600 second slice recipes; multi-account provisioning transport; and the launcher-enforced half of the own-worktree ruling.' package/register.md R15: 'The six orchestration pieces whose delete-when condition is met (detached spawn in the launcher, the wave-watch re-arm, the heartbeat, `harness_probe`, the quota poller and preflight check one, and the wave-watch new-session-id roll)'. package/children/C9.md and C15.md repeat R15's list.

findings.title: C9 shrinks the background-session trial from a three-account wave to one ordinary build
findings.body: Spec A FR-B6 requires the trial receipt to be 'one wave on that path across all three accounts, against the failure classes the machinery was built for, recorded in LEDGERS, run by hand on the harness primitives with no replacement code written first.' C9 What instead says 'One real build run as a background session of the host (claude --bg)'. C9 DoD grades a single ordinary-size build to a ready PR and never mentions three accounts, the failure classes, LEDGERS, or the no-replacement-code-first constraint. C15's decommission is decide-by on that receipt (R15), so an underscoped trial authorizes the wrong deletions.
findings.suggestion: Restate C9 What and DoD as the spec trial: one wave, all three accounts, named failure classes, LEDGERS record, harness primitives only. Make those artifacts the DoD.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-B6: 'The receipt is the **background-session trial** … one wave on that path across all three accounts, against the failure classes the machinery was built for, recorded in LEDGERS, run by hand on the harness primitives with no replacement code written first.' package/children/C9.md What: 'One real build run as a background session of the host (claude --bg)'. DoD: 'A build issue of ordinary size was run to a ready PR as a background session'.

findings.title: C15 deletes the usage poller; Spec A FR-B6 requires it parked, not deleted
findings.body: Spec A FR-B6 *Acceptance (record, quota retired outright)* says 'The usage poller is parked, not deleted. Preflight check one, the launch doctrine's quota leg, the "suspect quota" recovery section, and their tests come out in the decommission child'. C15 DoD requires the opposite: 'The quota poller, preflight check one, the quota leg of the launch doctrine, and the recovery section are gone; a grep for quota in the plugin returns only the glossary's history note.' A parked poller would still contain the word quota, so that grep forces deletion. C15 What also folds the poller into the 'six pieces' that leave. Builders following C15 will delete what the spec parks.
findings.suggestion: Split C15: delete preflight check one, the quota leg, and the recovery section; park the usage poller. Drop the grep-for-quota DoD or except the parked module.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-B6: 'quota exhaustion is no longer a thing the plugin watches. The usage poller is parked, not deleted. Preflight check one, the launch doctrine's quota leg, the "suspect quota" recovery section, and their tests come out in the decommission child'. package/children/C15.md DoD: 'The quota poller, preflight check one, the quota leg of the launch doctrine, and the recovery section are gone; a grep for quota in the plugin returns only the glossary's history note.'

findings.title: C4 What keeps CONVENTIONS parity sentences the spec and R13 retire
findings.body: Spec A FR-F4 *Acceptance (rule)*: 'The parity sentences go ("the same methodology, no behavior changes"; "bare `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` fails on Codex").' Register R13: 'a host that cannot carry one gets a disclosed absence, never a parity sentence.' C4 What tells the builder to narrow sections 7.1, 7.2, and 7.4 'keeping the existing parity sentences (the same methodology, no behavior changes) as the statement of the Codex position'. C4 DoD then requires the opposite: 'CONVENTIONS section 7 contains no parity sentence and states the Codex absence in the three-part form of register entry R13.' A builder following What lands the sentences the spec removed; a vet following DoD fails that landing. That is the wrong host position.
findings.suggestion: Delete the 'keeping the existing parity sentences' clause from C4 What so What matches FR-F4, R13, and the existing DoD.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-F4: 'The parity sentences go ("the same methodology, no behavior changes"; "bare `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` fails on Codex").' package/register.md R13: 'never a parity sentence'. package/children/C4.md What: 'keeping the existing parity sentences (the same methodology, no behavior changes) as the statement of the Codex position'. C4 DoD: 'CONVENTIONS section 7 contains no parity sentence'.

findings.title: Seven children quote R28 though R28 does not name them as consumers
findings.body: R28 *Consumers:* 'every child that touches tests (C3, C5, C7, C10, C11, C12, C13, C14, C15, C16)'. Those ten all quote R28. C1, C2, C4, C6, C8, C9, and C17 also quote R28 verbatim and are not on that list. C1's DoD retires verbatim-sentence pins; C2's What reconciles test_disposition_flow.py. Both touch tests, so the consumer list is incomplete rather than the extra quotes being accidental. The other extras quote a delete-on-contact rule the register does not bind them to. No named consumer fails to quote R28. Quoted R28 text matches register.md.
findings.suggestion: Add C1 and C2 (and any other test-touching child) to R28's Consumers line, or drop R28 quotes from children that do not touch tests.
findings.evidence: package/register.md R28 Consumers: 'C3, C5, C7, C10, C11, C12, C13, C14, C15, C16'. package/children/C1.md, C2.md, C4.md, C6.md, C8.md, C9.md, C17.md each contain the blockquote '**R28 — Delete on contact waits for the keep list.**' C1.md DoD: 'Every existing test that pinned verbatim sentences of the edited surfaces is retired under R4'. C2.md What: 'lib/tests/test_disposition_flow.py's worth-it-gate pins reconciled'.

findings.title: C12 DoD grades six-case answers against quotes that are not in the child body
findings.body: C12 DoD: 'The six-case suite is present as fixtures with expected receipts, and each case's expected answer matches Spec B FR-D8's six cases as quoted in this body.' The C12 body never quotes FR-D8's six cases (required seat recovered; required seat never recovered; reverted fix; stale cited head; Critical skipped or out of scope; mixed hand-landed and dispatched). A vet reading only the PR, its body, and CI cannot decide pass or fail against 'as quoted in this body' because the quote is absent. The What promises the six-case bite-proof; this DoD bullet does not make that promise gradable from the handback.
findings.suggestion: Quote Spec B FR-D8's six cases verbatim in C12, or change the DoD to name the six expected answers in the DoD bullets themselves.
findings.evidence: package/children/C12.md DoD: 'each case's expected answer matches Spec B FR-D8's six cases as quoted in this body.' The file's quoted register entries are R1, R5, R6, R7, R23, R24, R26, R27, R28; no FR-D8 six-case list appears in What or DoD. specs/spec-b-re-derivation.md FR-D8 lists the six cases at the 'the six cases' acceptance bullet.

findings.title: C14 and C15 both rewrite the launcher in Wave 3 with no ordering
findings.body: C14 What retires 'the launcher's hand-built argv' into the Claude engine adapter; its DoD is 'The launcher no longer builds a claude argv by hand: a grep for the old construction returns nothing'. C15 What deletes 'detached spawn in the launcher' as one of its six pieces, sequenced 'beside C14's argv retirement'. Coverage-map Wave 3 orders C14 after C11 and C15 after C9's receipt and does not order C14 relative to C15. R14 says C15's argv retirement 'is sequenced with' C14 but names no winner. Two Wave-3 children therefore give incompatible instructions on the same launcher surface with no merge order.
findings.suggestion: Make C15 after C14 (or fold argv retirement into one child) and state that only one child may edit the launcher spawn path.
findings.evidence: package/children/C14.md What: 'the launcher's hand-built argv retired into it'; DoD: 'The launcher no longer builds a claude argv by hand'. package/children/C15.md What: 'detached spawn in the launcher' leaves, 'Sequenced after C9's receipt and beside C14's argv retirement'. package/coverage-map.md Sequencing: 'C14 (after C11), C15 (after C9's receipt)'. package/register.md R14 Consumers: 'C15 (the launcher's argv retirement is sequenced with it)'.

findings.title: FR-B5.2 and FR-B5.3 splits copy C1's posture half, which does not cover envelope declaration
findings.body: Spec A FR-B5 *Acceptance (rule, declared variance)* requires every LLM-backed surface's contract doc to declare its variance envelope; *Acceptance (rule, the roster)* says the review loop and dispatch shell get theirs from Spec B's tables. The map splits both bullets identically: 'C1 owns the posture sentence in PHILOSOPHY; C10 owns the dispatch shell's declared envelope; C13 owns the review loop's'. The posture sentence is already FR-B5.1, owned wholly by C1. C1's declared half of FR-B5.2/3 therefore does not deliver envelope declaration. C10 and C13 can cover the two epic surfaces, but the split text assigns C1 a half it cannot be graded on for these criteria and repeats the same owner string on two distinct bullets.
findings.suggestion: Own FR-B5.2/3 as C10 (dispatch envelope) and C13 (review-loop envelope) only; leave posture on FR-B5.1 / C1.
findings.evidence: package/coverage-map.md lines 84–85 use the same Owner string for FR-B5 bullets 2 and 3, including 'C1 owns the posture sentence in PHILOSOPHY'. specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-B5.1 is already 'when a model-driven caller misses an exact token, the first ask is…' owned by C1 at line 83. FR-B5.2 is 'every LLM-backed surface's existing contract doc declares its variance envelope.'

findings.title: FR-F6 change 3 (delete on contact) is owned only by #1105; this epic's at-contact half has no owner
findings.body: Spec A FR-F6 numbered item 3 is the builder-at-contact rule: 'A behavior test that goes red under a builder's change is classified by the builder first' plus keep-list seeding. The map assigns the whole item to 'outside the epic: the verification-strategy spec's own children (#1105)'. #1105 can seed the keep list; it cannot perform this epic's builders' at-contact classification. R28 binds a subset of landing children to that rule, which is the reciprocal seam, but the coverage map itself still has no landing-child owner for the half this epic must deliver. That is a declared owner that cannot deliver its half.
findings.suggestion: Split FR-F6 n3: #1105 owns keep-list seed; every R28 consumer owns at-contact classification in this epic.
findings.evidence: specs/spec-a-doctrine.md FR-F6 item 3: 'A behavior test that goes red under a builder's change is classified by the builder first… The rule activates only once the keep list is stamped'. package/coverage-map.md line 137 Owner: 'outside the epic: the verification-strategy spec's own children (#1105), reciprocal seam R28'. package/register.md R28 Consumers are this epic's test-touching children, not #1105.

findings.title: C9 DoD requires a receipt 'in the format C15 quotes' but C15 defines no format
findings.body: C9 DoD: 'The receipt states, for each of the six pieces, needed or not needed with the evidence from the run, in the format C15 quotes.' C15 DoD only says each kept piece carries 'a restated delete-when condition quoting C9's receipt line for it' and does not quote or specify a receipt schema. A vet reading C9's PR/issue, its body, and CI cannot know which format passes. The What promises a piece-by-piece needed/not-needed receipt; this DoD bullet is not gradable from the handback.
findings.suggestion: Put the receipt fields (piece name, needed/not, evidence, restated delete-when) in C9 DoD and have C15 quote that list.
findings.evidence: package/children/C9.md DoD bullet 2: 'in the format C15 quotes'. package/children/C15.md DoD: 'kept with a restated delete-when condition quoting C9's receipt line for it' — no format block.

findings.title: C7 DoD 'no duty section exceeds one screen' is not a gradable artifact check
findings.body: C7 DoD requires every charter duty section to state rule and completion criterion and 'no duty section exceeds one screen'. Screen height is not an artifact a vet can read from the PR, its body, or CI. The rest of that bullet (rule, completion criterion, link, list of sections cut) is gradable.
findings.suggestion: Replace 'one screen' with a checkable bound (for example a stated line cap) or drop it; Spec A FR-B6 already forbids a line budget, so prefer 'each duty section states rule, completion criterion, and a pointer' only.
findings.evidence: package/children/C7.md DoD: 'no duty section exceeds one screen, and the PR body lists the sections cut.' Spec A FR-B6: 'there is no line budget and no knob count.'
